From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 01 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eval release decision matrix + action owners

Hi Anna / Harper (and internal team),

Thanks again for agreeing to run the pilot for PromptSet-4. Before we start the canary rollout I want to lock the decision matrix and owners so there are no surprises if we need to pause or roll back. Attached: eval-decision-matrix.xlsx (matrix with metric thresholds), promptset-sample-pack.zip (250 sample prompts from Acme flows), and an eval-metrics-template.csv for Acme's local results.

High-level asks:
- Can you confirm Acme's internal acceptance test owner and when they'll return the filled eval-metrics-template?
- Internal owners: please volunteer for the three action buckets below (technical rollout, quality signals, post-release audit).
- Agree the guardrail thresholds in the attached matrix or propose changes by EOD Aug 2.

Proposed quick thresholds (draft):
- Preference eval (pairwise A/B): new model must win >= +3 percentage points vs baseline across the primary prompt slice.
- Preference drift: if win-rate decreases by >4 points during canary window, auto-pause.
- Latency: p50 increase <= +100ms; p95 increase <= +250ms.
- Safety/hallucination: no increase in critical hallucination incidents (defined in matrix).

Proposed rollout lanes: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> full. Auto-hold if any guardrail exceeded.

Please reply with: owner names, any redlines to the thresholds, and whether Acme can deliver the filled CSV by Aug 4.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Product Manager, Evaluations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Tessa — quick technical notes and a couple of asks from infra: 

1) Canary routing: we can do 1/5/25/100% lanes but need to pin model variant names and quantization profile ahead of time. Please confirm whether the canary uses the same quantized artifact as prod or a "perf-optimized" build.

2) KV cache warm-up: the first 5k requests in canary will see higher latency until cache warms. Suggest excluding the first 500 requests from latency gating (we can mark these in logs).

3) Telemetry hooks: please add the exact event names you expect in the eval-metrics-template (e.g., eval.pairwise_choice, eval.hallucination_flag). We'll need those to set alerting.

4) Rollback automation: Jordan and I can wire the auto-pause script to the decision matrix but we need a single boolean flag in the spreadsheet ("auto_pause_enabled") and the HubSpot deal id to annotate the run.

I'll take technical rollout owner unless someone objects — will coordinate infra and feature flagging.

- Dev
Engineering, Serving Runtime

Adding the quality evaluation perspective. I reviewed the attached decision matrix and made inline comments (see Drive link below). Short summary of recommended acceptance criteria and signal definitions: 

- Primary metric: pairwise preference (human-labeled or preference model). Acceptance: +3 points median across the primary slice, and not worse than baseline across >70% of sub-slices.
- Secondary metrics: factuality score (automated checks + manual spot checks), instruction-following score, and hallucination incident rate. Define a "critical hallucination" as any output that fabricates a unique factual claim about customer data or business process.
- Stability window: evaluate both immediate canary window and 7-day moving average post-rollout. If the 7-day moving average of preference drops by >2 points after full rollout, we trigger a retrospective and potential revert.
- Canary plan suggestion: keep the first two lanes (1% and 5%) for signal sanity checks, require manual signoff to move to 25% unless automated metrics are clean.

Signal handoff: once Acme uploads the filled eval-metrics-template, our eval infra will run preference analysis and publish a short report (template: Drive link). Please make sure Acme's CSV has the required columns (prompt_id, baseline_choice, candidate_choice, metadata tags).

I'll own the quality signals/analysis and will post the first report within 48 hours of receiving the CSV.

Marissa Cole
Applied ML - Evaluations

Related doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3-eval-decision-matrix#comments

Thanks everyone — finalizing below with owners and actions. If anything here looks off please reply within 24 hours.

Summary (actionable):
- Technical rollout owner: Dev Patel — implement canary lanes, integrate auto-pause, exclude first 500 warm-up requests from latency checks. Due: Aug 6 internal smoke test.
- Quality signals & analysis owner: Marissa Cole — run preference analysis, produce first report within 48 hours of CSV ingestion. Due: within 48 hours after Aug 4.
- Acme eval owner / deliverable: Harper Lee — filled eval-metrics-template.csv, delivery by Aug 4 EOD. Note product freeze Aug 5-8; no moves to 25%+ in that window.
- Decision matrix flagging: Jordan Blake — add HubSpot deal id (HS-40932) and ensure JIRA-EVAL-789 is linked to runs. Due: Aug 5.

Rollback / pause rules (as agreed):
- Immediate auto-pause if pairwise win-rate decreases by >4 percentage points in a canary window.
- Manual hold if p50 latency increases by >100ms (post-warmup) or p95 >250ms.
- Critical hallucination incident: manual rollback and customer notification.

Next steps:
1) Harper uploads CSV by Aug 4.
2) Marissa ingests and posts report.
3) Dev runs internal smoke and turns on 1% canary when green.

Drive folder and matrix: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3-eval-decision-matrix
